findings.rationale: The two re-export lines expose `crate::fetch::FetchProviderFactory` and `crate::fetch::FetchProviderFactoryRegistry` as public paths. Repo-wide grep for those paths finds ZERO references outside `src/fetch/mod.rs` itself. The internal consumer (`src/fetch/registry.rs:2`) imports via the full `crate::fetch::factory::FetchProviderFactoryRegistry` path, which is independent of the re-export. The trait and registry struct themselves remain in the public `factory` submodule and continue to back the live registry pipeline — only the redundant top-level re-export aliases are removed, matching the skill's rule 'no live caller -> default CUT'. Note: the underlying `FetchProviderFactory`/`FetchProviderFactoryRegistry` types in factory.rs are KEPT — only the redundant top-level re-export aliases go.
findings.proposed_change: Removed `pub use factory::{FetchProviderFactory, FetchProviderFactoryRegistry};` from src/fetch/mod.rs:13. Updated the module doc-comment (line 4) to drop the rustdoc links to the now-private-at-top-level aliases; the underlying types remain reachable via `crate::fetch::factory::FetchProviderFactory` etc. and are documented as part of the `factory` submodule bullet.
findings.risk: None. No external crate or module referenced the re-exported paths (verified by grep across src/, bin/, interfaces/). Internal consumers use the full module path and are unaffected.
findings.verification: rg 'fetch::FetchProviderFactory' . --type rust -> empty. rg 'fetch::FetchProviderFactoryRegistry' . --type rust -> empty. Internal `factory.rs` references are within the defining module and unaffected by the re-export removal.

PROVIDER-TYPE NAME DRIFT (Form 5): 'crawl4ai' and 'firecrawl' strings are consistent across factory.rs:27,50, factory.rs:83-84, registry.rs:21,35, fetch_config.rs:413,447, crawl4ai.rs:6 (NAME const), firecrawl.rs:6 (NAME const). No drift. Wired.

DECIDE (out of scope, flagged for follow-up): src/builtin_tools/web_fetch/mod.rs:178 sets `extractor: Extractor::Crawl4ai` for ALL successful FetchProvider results — when a firecrawl provider serves the content, the persisted/extracted result still claims it came from Crawl4ai (the Extractor enum has only Readability/Selector/Crawl4ai variants, no Firecrawl). This is a real Form 5 name-drift bug at the consumer side of the FetchProvider contract, but it lives OUTSIDE src/fetch/ (in src/builtin_tools/web_fetch/types.rs and src/builtin_tools/web_fetch/mod.rs), so per the audit's 'Stay within src/fetch/' rule it is deferred to a follow-up task. Suggested fix: add `Firecrawl` variant to Extractor and map `provider.name()` -> enum at web_fetch/mod.rs:178.

DESIGN-PARALLEL NOTE: src/fetch mirrors src/search structurally (factory + registry + providers pattern). Search reuses the parallel `ProviderFactory` trait externally (config/validate.rs:480 calls `ProviderFactoryRegistry::with_defaults()` for validation; providers implement `crate::search::ProviderFactory`). Fetch does NOT have an equivalent external validator — fetch_config.rs uses the providers directly, not the factory registry. This is a deliberate design difference (fetch has only 2 providers, so no centralized validation is needed), not a defect.
